mission: Verify-pass per operator's 'don't trust verify' directive. Re-grounded in CLAUDE.md + CLAUDE_ROOT.md. Re-ran all four root gates plus tapit-attest tests fresh, all green. Adversarial code review of Phase 2.5 surface found one real bug: three call sites compute entry-digest as sha256(JSON.stringify(attestation)) instead of the canonical envelopeId(att) exported by tapit-attest. That breaks (1) determinism across engines, (2) OTS commit semantics, (3) URL stability across added signatures (Phase 2.6 witnesses would break every existing entry's URL), AND it duplicates a library responsibility. Fixing across createJournalEntry, JournalCard, JournalDetail. Other findings flagged in the close-out report, not fixed in this pass.

reason: Replaced sha256(JSON.stringify(signed)) with envelopeId(signed) from tapit-attest. Canonical content address per the library, deterministic, stable across added signatures (Phase 2.6 witness co-sign won't break entry URLs), and matches the digest the OTS proof actually commits to.
Same envelopeId() fix; dropped unused @noble/hashes/sha256 + local hex bytesToHex imports.
Same envelopeId() fix; lookup-by-digest in holdings now uses library function. Dropped sha256 + bytesToHex imports.

Added attach-anchors-on-confirm effect — subscribes to the anchor worker, when a row confirms with an anchor it finds the matching held attestation by envelopeId, replaces it with one carrying the anchor field, then debounces a 2-second wallet save so a flood of confirmations on app reopen produces one PBKDF2 cycle rather than N. Fixes a v1 correctness gap: backup/restore now preserves Bitcoin block heights.
